subject.title: [Feature]: Audit log for agent memory changes

question: Should OpenClaw implement memory mutation auditing as a core memory/security contract, expose a generic persistence-write plugin hook first, or leave this class of audit trail to external memory plugins?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but the permanent shape defines memory trust semantics, audit storage, privacy, tamper-evidence, and plugin boundaries, which need maintainer/security intent before implementation.

options.title: Design core memory audit contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical memory-specific design item and define an audited write path before accepting implementation PRs.

options.title: Start with persistence hook API
options.body: Route the first implementation through `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48509` so plugins can observe durable writes before a memory-specific ledger lands.

options.title: Leave to external memory systems
options.body: Treat Pinchy and world-model-mcp as external implementations and do not add OpenClaw core memory audit semantics now.

recommendation.title: Design core memory audit contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical memory-specific design item and define an audited write path before accepting implementation PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter already provided the prior maintainer-facing review keeping this open and has recent current-main ownership on the audit and memory write surfaces.
